identity.name: Jungian Model of the Psyche
identity.description: A theoretical model of the psyche associated with Carl Jung. The model describes consciousness, the personal unconscious, the collective unconscious, archetypes, psychic functions, psychological orientations, complexes, symbolic processes, psychological transformation and individuation.
The field of psychic contents that are currently available to awareness and capable of being related to the conscious standpoint of the individual.
The center of the field of consciousness and the organizing reference point through which conscious identity, continuity, attention and intentional experience are structured.
A psychic representation, perception, thought, feeling, memory or other content that is presently available to consciousness.
Selective allocation of conscious awareness toward particular contents, objects or processes.

The domain of psychic contents associated with the individual's personal history that are not currently conscious, including forgotten, repressed or insufficiently differentiated material and complexes.
Organized clusters of emotionally charged psychic contents associated around a particular theme, relationship, experience or concern.
A psychologically organized cluster of emotionally charged memories, representations, expectations, perceptions and behavioral tendencies.
A memory associated with the thematic and affective organization of a psychological complex.
A representation, image, belief or association organized around the theme of a complex.
An expectation or anticipatory pattern associated with a psychological complex.
Experiences belonging to the individual's personal history and contributing to the organization of personal psychic contents.
Stored or reconstructable representations of personally experienced events and information.
Personal psychic content that is excluded or insufficiently available to conscious awareness according to the theoretical model.
A theoretical layer of the psyche containing archetypal structures and potentials that Jung regarded as not derived solely from individual personal experience.
A family of recurring structural patterns within Jungian theory that organize psychic experience, symbolic imagery, affect and behavior.
A recurring structural pattern in Jungian theory capable of organizing perception, imagination, affect, interpretation and symbolic experience.
The archetypal representation of psychic totality and the organizing principle of the psyche as a whole within Jungian analytical psychology.
A psychological structure associated with the social role, presentation and adaptation of the individual to social expectations and situations.
A Jungian archetypal structure associated with aspects of personality that are insufficiently recognized, accepted or integrated by consciousness.
A Jungian archetypal concept concerning an unconscious psychic figure associated historically in Jung's model with the inner feminine image in a man's psyche.
A Jungian archetypal concept concerning an unconscious psychic figure associated historically in Jung's model with the inner masculine image in a woman's psyche.
An archetypal pattern associated with overcoming obstacles, differentiation, initiative and the development of conscious agency.
An archetypal pattern associated in Jungian interpretation with potentiality, development, renewal and emergent psychological wholeness.
An archetypal pattern associated with maternal containment, nourishment, origin, dependency, protection and transformation.
An archetypal pattern associated with authority, order, law, structure, guidance and transmission.
An archetypal pattern associated with contradiction, disruption, ambiguity, transformation and the destabilization of established psychological patterns.
An archetypal symbolic pattern associated with knowledge, guidance, insight and orientation.
An archetypal symbolic pattern associated with wisdom, intuition, guidance and transformation.
An archetypal pattern associated with origin, containment, nourishment, fertility, protection and potentially overwhelming dependence.
The four principal psychological functions described in Jung's typological model: thinking, feeling, sensation and intuition.
A psychological function concerned with conceptual differentiation, classification, logical relations and judgment through ideas.
A psychological function concerned with valuation, significance, preference and the determination of whether something is experienced as desirable, undesirable, acceptable or unacceptable.
A psychological function concerned with perception of concrete actuality and the qualities of what is directly experienced.
A psychological function concerned with perception of possibilities, implicit relationships, emerging patterns and meanings not necessarily derived from direct sensory observation.
The Jungian distinction between introversion and extraversion as orientations of psychic energy and attention.
An orientation in which psychic attention and valuation are primarily directed toward subjective experience and the individual's inner psychological world.
An orientation in which psychic attention and valuation are primarily directed toward objects, situations and the external environment.
Processes through which conscious and unconscious contents interact, influence one another, become activated, transformed or integrated.
A psychological process in which psychic contents associated with the subject are experienced as belonging to another person, object or situation.
A theoretical process in which unconscious activity tends to complement, balance or compensate for the one-sidedness of conscious attitudes.
A psychological process in which the ego or another psychic structure becomes strongly aligned with a role, image, group, object or psychic content.
A process through which previously undifferentiated psychological contents, functions or structures become more distinct and consciously recognizable.
A process through which differentiated psychic contents become related within a more coherent psychological organization.
A process through which psychological experience becomes represented through symbolic images, narratives, metaphors or other symbolic forms.
A process through which a previously latent psychic structure or content becomes psychologically active and capable of influencing experience.
A Jungian term for the activation of a particular psychic complex or configuration in response to a situation, stimulus or psychological condition.
Psychological processes involving symbolic images, dreams, myths, fantasies and active imagination.
A symbolic representation that expresses psychological meaning not exhausted by its immediately apparent literal or conceptual interpretation.
A symbolic psychological experience occurring during sleep that may contain images, affects, narratives and transformations of psychic material.
A culturally transmitted symbolic narrative that can express recurring archetypal themes and patterns of psychological meaning.
An imaginative psychic experience involving internally generated images, narratives, scenarios or possibilities.
A Jungian method of engaging consciously with spontaneously emerging images, fantasies and other unconscious material while maintaining a relationship with conscious awareness.

A developmental process in Jungian psychology through which differentiated and previously unconscious aspects of the psyche become increasingly related within a more integrated psychological totality.

A process of becoming consciously related to aspects of personality represented by the Shadow and potentially incorporating previously unrecognized contents into conscious psychological understanding.
The psychological relationship between the conscious ego and the archetypal Self within Jungian theory.
The conceptual totality of conscious and unconscious psychic structures and processes represented within the Jungian model.
Psychic content that is not currently within conscious awareness in the Jungian model.
An event, perception, association, memory or situation capable of activating a previously latent psychological configuration or complex.
Psychic material participating in a projection process.
A person, object, situation or representation onto which projected psychic content is experienced as belonging.
The interpersonal, cultural and social environment within which the individual performs roles and establishes relationships.

relation-type.description: Indicates structural inclusion of one object or component within another.
Indicates structural membership in a larger system.
Indicates that one psychological structure or process may affect another.
Indicates activation of a psychic structure or process.
Indicates a complementary or balancing relationship between psychic attitudes or contents.
Indicates that one structure functions as an intermediary between other structures or domains.
Indicates symbolic or psychological expression of content.
Indicates manifestation through a symbolic or experiential form.
Indicates incorporation of differentiated contents into a more coherent psychological organization.
Indicates external attribution of psychic content.
Indicates representation of psychological content by symbolic form.
Indicates activation of a complex or psychic configuration.
Indicates psychological tension or opposition between differentiated contents or attitudes.
Indicates a complementary relationship between psychic structures or attitudes.
Indicates psychological change from one organization, state or configuration to another.

state.name: Inactive
state.description: A psychic structure is not currently strongly activated.

state.name: Activated
state.description: A psychic structure is currently psychologically active.

state.name: Dominant
state.description: A psychic structure has become especially influential within current psychological experience.

state.name: Integrating
state.description: A psychic structure or content is participating in a process of conscious psychological integration.

state.name: Integrated
state.description: A psychic content or structure has become more coherently related to conscious psychological organization.

state.name: Decentered
state.description: Not occupying the ordinary central position of conscious ego awareness.

state.name: Expanded
state.description: Experientially expanded beyond an ordinary narrow conscious focus.

state.name: Ongoing
state.description: A developmental or psychological process is continuing.

state.name: Developing
state.description: A psychological structure or relationship is undergoing development or differentiation.
